title: Mortgage Rates Break Above 7% After the Fed's September Hike; Daily 30-Year at 7.24% and Jumbo at 7.40%
summary: Borrowing costs jumped sharply this week. The Federal Reserve raised rates at its September 16 meeting, and the benchmark 10-year Treasury yield pushed to roughly 5 percent - its highest level in about two decades - as an oil-price spike tied to the Iran conflict lifted inflation expectations. Daily lender surveys followed: Mortgage News Daily put the average 30-year conforming fixed at 7.24 percent and the 30-year jumbo at 7.40 percent on September 16-17, a one-year high and well above the 5.99 percent 2026 low. Freddie Mac's weekly PMMS survey, which lags daily pricing by several days, still read 6.76 percent for the week ended September 10; the next PMMS print is due September 17 and is expected to close much of that gap. For South Florida, where cash accounted for 37.8 percent of Miami-Dade closings and 35.9 percent of Broward closings in August, the move widens the advantage for cash and high-end buyers and raises the cost of financing on leveraged multifamily and commercial acquisitions.

title: August County Data: SE Florida Single-Family Medians Keep Rising While Listings Fall About 20% - Miami-Dade $680K, Broward $650K, Palm Beach $650K
summary: MIAMI REALTORS + RWorld released August 2026 county statistics on September 16. Single-family median sale prices rose year-over-year in every SE Florida county: Miami-Dade to $680,000 (+3.8%), Broward to $650,000 (+4.0%), Palm Beach to $650,000 (+3.2%), Martin to $656,900 (+12.8%) and St. Lucie to $402,500 (+0.6%). Condo medians were mixed - Broward $257,500 (+4.0%), Palm Beach $300,000 (+5.3%), Martin $277,500 (+20.7%) and St. Lucie $320,000 (+7.2%), while Miami-Dade slipped 0.5% to $408,000. Single-family closed sales softened almost everywhere (Miami-Dade -3.1%, Palm Beach -2.0%, Martin -11.3%, St. Lucie -6.5%; Broward flat at +0.1%), ending an 11-month streak of year-over-year gains. The supply story is the tighter constraint: single-family active listings fell 19.2% in Miami-Dade, 22.5% in Broward, 23.8% in Palm Beach and 21.8% in Martin. Months' supply of single-family inventory sits at 4.9 in Miami-Dade and 4.1 in Broward - seller's-market territory - while existing condos remain a buyer's market at 12.1 and 9.9 months. Statewide, Florida Realtors reported 21,497 single-family closings (-1.4%) at a $415,000 median (+1.2%), with active listings down 13.0%.

title: 13th Floor and Wexford Win Approval for a 30-Story, 350-Unit Flagler Village Tower in Fort Lauderdale
summary: The Fort Lauderdale City Commission approved the site plan for Flagler Village Residences, a 30-story, 350-unit rental tower at 500 Northeast 3rd Avenue just north of downtown. The project adds about 3,500 square feet of retail and a seven-story podium with 512 parking spaces. Miami-based 13th Floor Investments, led by managing principal Arnaud Karsenti, is developing with West Palm Beach-based Wexford Real Estate Investors; the partnership assembled the 1.37-acre site in parcel buys between 2007 and 2019 for a combined $5.49 million. The commission granted a deviation allowing a 17,669-square-foot floorplate - 41 percent above the 12,500-square-foot by-right maximum - and separately vacated a 150-by-15-foot city alley bisecting the site. The approval lands in a softening rental market: Marcus & Millichap notes Fort Lauderdale's rental vacancy tightened from 5.1 to 4.8 percent in the 12 months through March, the fastest among major Florida markets, but affordability pressure and concession use continue to temper rent growth.

title: Memorial Healthcare Pays $69M for Hollywood's 254,000 SF Venture Center, Becoming Its Own Office Landlord
summary: South Broward Hospital District, doing business as Memorial Healthcare System, bought the three-building, 254,000-square-foot Venture Center office complex at 200-300 South Park Road and 3440 Hollywood Boulevard for $69 million - $272 per square foot - from entities tied to Fox Ridge Capital and Jackson Land Development. The complex last traded at $50 million in 2021, a 38 percent gain in five years. Cushman & Wakefield's Scott O'Donnell, Dominic Montazemi, Mike Davis and team represented the sellers; CBRE's Chris Lee and Will Portfolio brought the buyer. Memorial already leased space in the 16-acre complex, which sits three blocks from its flagship Memorial Regional Hospital. CEO Shane Strum told the South Florida Business Journal the system plans to relocate administrative offices there and would eventually like to occupy all three buildings, without forcing out current tenants. The deal follows Baptist Health's $53.5 million Coconut Creek Kohl's purchase and comes as Broward's medical office market cooled in the second quarter - sales volume dipped and vacancy rose to 12.5 percent per Colliers - even as rents and leasing held up. Healthcare owner-users continue to be the most aggressive bidders for well-located Broward office product.

title: Bugatti to Brand a 60-Story, 183-Unit Condo Tower on the Miami River - Its First in the U.S.
summary: French hypercar maker Bugatti will brand Prosper Group and Versluys Group's planned 60-story tower at 75 Southwest Miami Avenue Road, the first Bugatti-branded residential project in the United States. The developers paid $50 million for the one-acre site in August, a year and a half after going under contract; the parcel was part of Newgard Development Group and Two Roads Development's One Brickell Riverfront assemblage and carries more than 300 feet of Miami River frontage. The unit count rises to 183 condos including four penthouses, up from a previously planned 158, and the project is valued at roughly $650 million. Sales are expected to launch in the first half of 2027. Douglas Elliman had been expected to lead sales and marketing but is no longer involved. The tower deepens South Florida's lead as the U.S. capital of branded residences, alongside Bentley, Pagani, Aston Martin and Porsche Design towers - though brokers increasingly question how many more brand deals the market can absorb.

title: Mount Vernon Pays $66.9M for a Publix-Anchored Palm Beach Gardens Center in Its First South Florida Retail Buy
summary: Boston-based Mount Vernon Company paid $66.9 million - $321 per square foot - for the 207,900-square-foot Promenade Shopping Plaza at 9810 Alternate A1A in Palm Beach Gardens. Seller Nuveen Real Estate cleared $17.6 million over the $49.3 million it paid in 2017. Beacon Bank provided a $35.9 million acquisition loan. The 1989-vintage strip sits on about 22.8 acres, is 98 percent occupied, and is anchored by a Publix that reopened after renovations last year, with Planet Fitness, Goodwill and Ace Hardware among the other tenants; the county assessed it at $49 million this year. JLL's Danny Finkle, Jorge Portela and Kim Flores represented Nuveen. Mount Vernon, led by chairman Bruce Percelay, says it plans to hold long term - its first major South Florida shopping center acquisition. The sale runs counter to Nuveen's recent direction: the TIAA affiliate raised $330 million for its U.S. Cities Retail Fund this year and bought the Aldi-anchored Coral Landings III in Margate for $46.3 million in April. Grocery-anchored retail remains the most liquid commercial asset class in Palm Beach County.

title: Everglades Island Waterfront Trades at $40M - 158% Above Its 2019 Price and $6,765 Per Foot
summary: Palm Beach philanthropist and art collector Kimberly Bluhm, buying through a land trust, paid $40 million for the 5,900-square-foot waterfront house at 608 Island Drive on Everglades Island - $6,765 per square foot. Sellers Roger and Raisa Webb had paid $15.5 million in 2019, making the trade a 158 percent gain in seven years. The 0.44-acre intracoastal lot holds five bedrooms and six and a half baths; the home was completed in 2019 after homebuilder Bruce Malasky bought the property for $6.5 million in 2016. It was listed in June at $41 million. Sotheby's Carole Koeppel represented the seller and Christian Angle the buyer. Bluhm, married to billionaire real estate and casino investor Neil Bluhm, also owns a Palm Beach condo bought for $7.4 million in 2020. Everglades Island continues to clear at extraordinary pricing - 757 Island Drive sold for $93.3 million in May and the vacant lot at 690 Island Drive fetched $39.2 million in June - while Angle's $195 million Billionaires Row listing at 1616 South Ocean Boulevard tests the top of the market.

title: Goldman Sachs Pays $154.5M for a 397-Unit Davie Rental at $389,169 Per Door; Kerra Buys Pompano's Aviara East for $73M
summary: Two Broward apartment complexes traded as South Florida multifamily investment sales regain momentum. A Goldman Sachs affiliate paid $154.5 million for the 397-unit Modera Academical Village I at 3440 SW 76th Terrace in Davie, buying from Boca Raton-based Mill Creek Residential, which completed the eight-story, 3.1-acre project last year - $389,169 per door. In Pompano Beach, Aviara Properties sold the 228-unit Aviara East Pompano at 1611 S Dixie Highway to Orlando-based Kerra Investments for $73 million, or $320,175 per unit; Kerra, led by Revital and Eliav Kling, assumed the seller's debt and increased it to $58 million with Ladder Capital as lender. First-half South Florida multifamily deal volume hit $2.5 billion, up 19.4 percent year-over-year per Avison Young, though brokers caution some reflects late-2025 contracts closing now. Leasing finally outpaced deliveries - 13,774 units leased versus 12,751 completed in the 12 months through Q2 per CoStar - but roughly 28,000 more units are due by late next year. Realtor.com put South Florida's July median asking rent at $2,279, down 1.3 percent year-over-year.

title: Redfearn Capital Locks Up Delray Beach's East Atlantic Avenue with $42.2M in Back-to-Back Retail Buys
summary: Alex Redfearn's Delray Beach-based Redfearn Capital paid a combined $42.2 million for two commercial properties on East Atlantic Avenue, among the largest commercial deals in the town's history. The firm paid $38.2 million at auction for the 22,800-square-foot office and retail property at 105-111 East Atlantic Avenue - $1,674 per square foot - with tenants including Sloan's Ice Cream and Geronimo Tequila Bar and Southwest Grill; Cushman & Wakefield's Ron Granite and Jason Hochman arranged financing. In a separate $4 million deal it bought the renovated 1,960-square-foot 1950-built retail building at 123 East Atlantic Avenue from William R. Burke, who paid $173,000 in 1996, for $2,040 per square foot. The larger sale followed a lawsuit settlement between the former co-owners, the estate of late TMP Worldwide CEO David Hosokawa and bakery owner Billy Himmelrich, who jointly sold and split proceeds. Redfearn paid $10 million for 131 East Atlantic Avenue in December, giving it a contiguous swath of Atlantic Avenue frontage, and last month flipped a Palm Beach office-retail building at 317 Peruvian Avenue for $18 million, a $10 million gain in a year.

title: Galium Capital Buys North Miami Beach's 156-Unit Arbors Aventura for $28.7M in a Value-Add Play
summary: Miami-based Galium Capital, led by Jacques Bessoudo and Iser Rabinovitz, acquired the 156-unit Arbors Aventura at 2365 NE 173rd Street in North Miami Beach for roughly $28.7 million excluding furniture and fixtures, with Newmark's Tal Frydman representing both sides. The 1969-built complex of three three-story buildings last sold for $35.2 million in 2022 to Mavik Capital Management, Triangle Capital Group and Corinthian Capital Real Estate Partners as part of an $82 million three-property portfolio - so the trade prints well below the prior basis. Galium, founded in 2018 with more than $750 million in assets under management and over $600 million of multifamily volume across Texas, Maryland and Tampa, plans renovations to lift value. The buy lands amid a North Miami Beach and North Miami building boom of about 11,500 units in construction or planning, including PPG Development's 728-unit project and LeFrak and Turnberry's SoLe Mia, which may reach 4,400 units and 1.5 million square feet of commercial space at full buildout.

title: Related Ross Buys the 124-Acre Boca Raton Innovation Campus, Entitled for a 1,243-Unit Micro-City
summary: Steve Ross' Related Ross acquired BRiC, the 1.7 million-square-foot former IBM headquarters at 5000 T Rex Avenue between Yamato Road and I-95, in the firm's first Boca Raton deal. Price was not disclosed; the seller, an entity linked to Boca Raton-based CP Group, paid $320.2 million for the 124-acre campus in 2021, and Ares Commercial Real Estate Services provided acquisition financing. CP Group won zoning approval in 2023 for up to 1,243 residential units, a 140-room hotel, 125,000 square feet of retail, 85,000 square feet of medical office and a 55,000-square-foot entertainment venue; Related plans to keep the office and tech building while adding retail and amenities. D-Wave Quantum is moving its headquarters from Palo Alto to the campus by year-end. The buy follows Ross' $28.3 million Wellington land purchase in August and deepens the Palm Beach County office and mixed-use pipeline.

title: Mortgage Rates Rise a Second Straight Week to 6.76%; 15-Year at 6.09% and Jumbo Near 6.85%
summary: Freddie Mac's Primary Mortgage Market Survey put the 30-year fixed at 6.76% for the week ended September 10, up from 6.71%, with the 15-year fixed at 6.09% versus 6.04%. A year ago the 30-year averaged 6.35%, so financing is now roughly 40 basis points more expensive than last September. The daily 30-year jumbo average moved to about 6.85% from roughly 6.78%, leaving the jumbo-to-conforming spread near 9 basis points. Two consecutive increases modestly raise debt service on leveraged acquisitions and tighten cash-on-cash math on income deals underwritten at summer rates.

title: Longpoint Pays $195M for a 10-Building, 730,000 SF Miami-Dade Small-Bay Industrial Portfolio at $267 Per Foot
summary: Boston-based Longpoint Partners, one of South Florida's most active warehouse owners, bought 730,000 square feet of small-bay space across 10 buildings on 42 acres in Miami-Dade industrial submarkets. The portfolio was 90% leased at closing with 74 tenants averaging close to 10,000 square feet each; buildings average 73,000 square feet. Seller and addresses were not disclosed. Industrial was South Florida's strongest commercial asset class in the first half, with 193 deals totaling $3.3 billion, a 130.5% jump from last year per Avison Young. Miami-Dade tenants leased 3 million square feet in the second quarter (7.4 million year to date) and net absorption reached 783,000 square feet, reversing three straight negative quarters, with asking rents at $17 per foot, up 1.5% year over year per Colliers.

title: Terra and Frisbie Add 26 Acres of the Former Palm Beach Kennel Club for $19.5M, Advancing 1,145 Apartments
summary: Miami-based Terra and Palm Beach-based Frisbie Group paid $19.5 million, or about $1.44 million per acre, for 26.1 acres at 1111 North Congress Avenue, buying from Investment Corporation of Palm Beach. It is their third purchase at the defunct dog track after $20.9 million in 2025 and $7.79 million in June, assembling 42 acres in unincorporated Palm Beach County near the airport. The partners applied in 2024 to rezone the land for 1,145 multifamily units plus 120,000 square feet of retail and other commercial space in a community called Westgate Village, with construction expected to start this year. It is one of the larger rental pipelines moving forward in central Palm Beach County.

title: Miami Commission Moves to Put Short-Term Rentals Under a Microscope After Brickell 'Animal House' Complaints
summary: District 2 Commissioner Damian Pardo's resolution, set for a Thursday vote, would direct the city manager to scrutinize vacation rentals citywide and deliver quarterly updates on condo buildings with repeat violations, plus a city attorney report on how other cities have handled short-term rental registration since 2011. The trigger was The Club at Brickell Bay, nicknamed the "Animal House" after partying vacationers drew resident complaints. Rentals of under 30 days remain legal across Miami, but zoning dictates where lodging is allowed by right, requires additional approval, or is prohibited, and STRs must hold certificates of occupancy and use plus a state lodging license. Developer Ricardo Dunin of North Development, who builds purpose-built STR condos under hospitality zoning (most recently Domus Brickell Park), backs the effort and says enforcement, not the rules, is the gap. Investor read: condo-to-income plays in buildings without lodging entitlements carry rising enforcement risk, while hospitality-zoned product does not.

title: Pebb Capital Lands $223M Refi on Delray Beach's 97%-Leased Sundy Village
summary: JPMorgan Chase and Hudson Bay Capital provided the $223 million loan, replacing a $173 million 2023 construction loan from JPMorgan and Monroe Capital, which is stepping away from the project; Walker & Dunlop arranged the new financing. Phase one at 22 West Atlantic Avenue is a 7-acre development with 100,000 square feet of office, 30,000 square feet of retail and 268 parking spaces, completed in 2025 and now 97 percent pre-leased to tenants including Fairstead Development, Industrious and Vertical Bridge, with Van Leeuwen Ice Cream, Maman, Barcelona Wine Bar and Double Knot on the retail side. The next phase adds a 79,141-square-foot office at 100 Southeast First Avenue leased to Boca Raton-based DigitalBridge, a 165-space garage and 3,400 square feet of retail. Todd Rosenberg's Boca Raton-based Pebb began assembling the land in 2019 for $40 million, and has added a $70 million Miami Beach office building and a $72.5 million Design District stake this year.
